Subject: Re: AP onboarding — payment route and constraints

Hi Jane — thanks again for the time on today's call. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side: 

- Recap of what we learned:
  • NovaMed requires vendor onboarding for any new supplier; AP sign-off needed for vendors receiving invoices.
  • For purchases > $10k AP prefers PO-backed invoices; smaller purchases can be paid by corporate card if vendor onboarding is complete.
  • AP will need W9 (or equivalent), a primary contact, and SOC 2 attestation or equivalent security docs for data-bearing integrations.

- Commercial paths we discussed:
  1) PO + standard MSA -> invoice cadence (Net 30) — typical procurement route, timeline ~2–3 weeks for onboarding and PO issuance.
  2) Card/marketplace pilot — faster to go live (card billing), but requires either a marketplace listing (AWS/GCP) or vendor accepted card processing; may need different agreement & fees.

- Actions / ask from NovaMed:
  • Can you share the AP contact and the vendor onboarding form (if available)?
  • Confirm whether SOC 2 self-attestation is acceptable or if you require full report.
  • Which path would you prefer us to prepare materials for first (PO route vs. card/pilot)?

I attached a short vendor onboarding checklist (redwood-vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf) and a one-page payment options summary (payment-options-summary.xlsx). If you prefer, we can prepare a redlineable MSA + sample invoice for the PO path.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Diego — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from AP / procurement side: 

- PO vs card policy:
  • Any single-year SaaS commitment > $10,000 requires a PO and our signed MSA.
  • Card is allowed for transactional purchases or pilots under $10,000 if vendor has an active vendor record and a W9 on file.

- Required vendor artifacts for onboarding: W9 (US vendors), evidence of security posture (SOC2 Type II or SOC2 self-attestation + controls summary), vendor contact for billing, and a completed vendor onboarding form.

- Timeline expectations: Once we have a completed vendor form + W9 + MSA countersigned, PO issuance typically takes 7–10 business days.

I've attached our vendor form so your legal/finance team can pre-fill it (Novamed_vendor_form.pdf). 

For next steps: please send the pre-filled vendor form + W9 and a draft MSA (or a link to a marketplace subscription if you want to pursue faster card billing). Otherwise we'll proceed with PO route.

Thanks,
Jane Lopez
Sr. Manager, Procurement — NovaMed Analytics

Diego / Marissa — quick internal note on strategy before we reply to Jane: 

- If NovaMed prefers PO (likely, given the >$10k threshold), we should accelerate:
  1) Pre-fill their vendor form, attach our W9, and provide SOC2 self-attestation + link to SOC2 report for legal to review.
  2) Send a redlineable MSA with the PO/invoice schedule filled in. Offer Net 30 as standard; be prepared to discuss 45 in unusual cases.

- Alternate faster path: Marketplace or card pilot. We have an AWS Marketplace listing option but it takes 2–3 business days to activate for a specific seller + customer if paperwork is in order. Marketplace would allow them to pay by card (or consolidated billing) and can accelerate time to value if they want to start with an initial pilot below $10k.

Recommendation: prepare both packets (PO path + marketplace pilot summary) and let Jane choose — include cost/terms differences and onboarding time estimates. I can draft the marketplace checklist and partner contact if needed.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Programs | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jane — and thanks Karthik for the plan. 

Jane, attaching the pre-filled vendor form + our W9 and a short payment-options spreadsheet to make the tradeoffs explicit (attachment: payment-options-summary.xlsx). Summary below: 

Option A — PO / MSA (recommended if you want standard procurement control)
 • Requirements: completed vendor form, W9, countersigned MSA, SOC2 attestation.
 • Timeline: vendor record + PO issuance ~7–10 business days after we return documents.
 • Billing: monthly invoice per PO schedule, Net 30.

Option B — Marketplace / Card pilot (faster start)
 • Requirements: marketplace subscription or vendor acceptance of card; may require additional marketplace terms & fee structure.
 • Timeline: can be live within 2–4 business days if marketplace activation and billing setup are complete.
 • Tradeoffs: faster but may have different billing cadence and small marketplace fees.

Next suggested steps: 
1) We will return the completed vendor form and W9 by EOD today.
2) Please confirm AP contact to receive PO docs (you mentioned ap.procure@novamed.com — can you confirm?).
3) If PO route is preferred, we will send a redlineable MSA and a proposed invoice schedule (weekly/monthly) — would Net 30 be acceptable?

Quoted from your note: 
> "Once we have a completed vendor form + W9 + MSA countersigned, PO issuance typically takes 7–10 business days."

We will target the PO path unless you indicate you prefer the marketplace/card pilot. 

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
